facts.state_of_play:
At a Senate hearing Wednesday, Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment 111 times. Republican Sen. Rand Paul led the hearing and said there is a "very real chance" Fauci could be prosecuted. A Senate committee plans a contempt vote next week. Fauci's private notes were also a subject of scrutiny. Legal experts called the Fifth Amendment strategy sound but politically damaging, and the Biden pardon may be tested. Trump said he watched the entire 3-hour-plus hearing.

Separately, Todd Blanche's attorney general nomination is in jeopardy ahead of a Thursday Senate judiciary committee vote. Senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis are threatening to block the nomination unless DOJ provides written assurances that a $1.8bn anti-weaponization slush fund tied to a Trump-IRS settlement is dead and that audit immunity for Trump and his family is narrowed. A seven-figure settlement to Trump allies was announced two days before the vote. Epstein survivor Dani Bensky also alleged Blanche told survivors to "get to the point" in a DOJ meeting.

facts.state_of_play: Iran launched ballistic missiles in an attempted surprise attack on US military installations in the Middle East; the US says it thwarted the attack. Trump threatened severe retaliation. A drone struck a US-owned gas storage tanker at Egypt's Damietta port. Oil prices surged 7% above $90/barrel. US oil inventories are at precariously low levels. Internally, Trump is exasperated as top officials cannot agree on an Iran strategy. The Federal Reserve, chaired by Kevin Warsh, voted 9-3 to hold interest rates steady for the fifth consecutive time, keeping the federal funds rate at 3.5%–3.75%; three members dissented in favor of a quarter-point hike, the first three-dissent vote in a decade. US borrowing costs are at a 19-year high. The Dow closed down over 1,000 points on the news. The hold is seen as a win for Trump, though it contrasts with Warsh's own hawkish rhetoric. F1 is weighing moving its season-closing Middle East races to Europe, with a mid-September decision deadline. Separately, Trump announced a $22.5 billion redesign of Dulles International Airport. In football governance, FIFA President Gianni Infantino has announced a plan to create a new subsidiary to run part of the World Cup and sell a 20% stake to private investors in a venture valued at $20bn, with Joshua Kushner named as the investor; federations have until September 19 to decide. The plan has triggered furious backlash: UEFA has called an emergency meeting of its 55 members for Thursday to coordinate a response, with a European boycott of FIFA tournaments including the Women's World Cup under consideration. During the World Cup, US federal authorities seized 44 drones and $9 million in fake FIFA merchandise in Houston.

facts.state_of_play: Microsoft and Meta both reported quarterly earnings for the period ended June 30, 2026. Microsoft beat expectations with $90B revenue and $35.8B net income, logging a $3.2B gain on its Anthropic investment while its OpenAI stake was a mixed result; MSFT rose 3%+ after hours. Meta posted $60.8B in Q2 revenue (+28% YoY) but free cash flow collapsed 91% YoY to $784M and it raised capex guidance to $130B-$145B, sending META down ~10% after hours. Separately, SpaceX is active on multiple launch fronts: NASA confirmed the Roman Space Telescope will launch Aug. 30 on a Falcon Heavy; the US Space Force awarded SpaceX a $1.6B contract for 18 Falcon 9 missions through 2027; and SpaceX is set to launch a secret US government reconnaissance satellite early July 30.
